prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Mixed · Multilingual glossary (language en).
Grid: 5 columns × 6 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "English" · longest unbreakable word 76px · one-line width 165px
  col 2: header "中文" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 62px
  col 3: header "日本語" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 107px
  col 4: header "한국어" · longest unbreakable word 13px · one-line width 73px
  col 5: header "العربية" · longest unbreakable word 44px · one-line width 112px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 360px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"A five-language glossary for translators/writers: one English source term per row, with parallel translations in Chinese, Japanese, Korean and Arabic. Its job is lookup and cross-language comparison, not numeric analysis.","reading":"The eye anchors on the English column (col 1) to find the term, then sweeps right across the four translation columns, comparing the same row across scripts. Rows must read as units, so no column may be so narrow that a row becomes a ragged multi-line tower while its neighbours are one line.","groups":["cols 2–5 (中文, 日本語, 한국어, العربية) form one parallel group of equal-role translation columns; they should share a common rhythm even though their scripts differ in width","col 1 (English) is the anchor/key column and should be visually dominant over the translations"],"keep_intact":["Arabic words in col 5, especially the 44px unbreakable token — col 5 must get at least ~65px so no Arabic word splits mid-word","English words in col 1 (longest unbreakable 76px) — col 1 must stay ≥ ~97px so 'Horizontal' never breaks","All CJK single terms (表格, 表, 표) which are short and must not be split into stray characters by over-narrow columns"],"may_wrap":["Multi-word English phrases ('Horizontal scrolling', 'Column width allocation') — natural wrap at the space, absorbed by existing row height","Japanese and Chinese terms (横スクロール, 横向滚动, 列幅の割り当て) — these wrap cleanly at character boundaries","Korean phrases (가로 스크롤, 열 너비 할당) — wrap at the space between eojeol","Arabic phrases — wrap at word boundaries as long as each word fits"]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[146,50,50,45,68],"idea":"Anchor-first: give English nearly half the width so source terms read as whole phrases, and let the four short-script translations absorb the squeeze by wrapping at character/word boundaries."},{"name":"B","widths":[114,43,74,51,77],"idea":"Proportional: scale every column by the same ~0.69 factor of its natural one-line width, preserving the table's original width rhythm so each column wraps by a comparable amount."},{"name":"C","widths":[100,55,70,50,84],"idea":"Translation-priority: shrink English to just above its longest word (always two lines) and spend the savings on the translation columns, giving Japanese and Arabic enough room to keep most phrases to two lines."}]}
